Theme

School & learning

poetry noun

also verse, poems, poetic, write poetry, poem, write a poem

classical

Cic. Or. 70: poēmata opposed to ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 3.15 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 30: poēma, poēmatis n., a poem

poēmata, poēmatum n. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

poems, poetry (as opposed to prose)

Poetry as a body of poems; the singular poēma, poēmatis n. is one poem.

Other words

  • poētica, poēticae f. — the art of poetry

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.69: ō praeclāram ēmendātrīcem vītae poēticam! (Lewis & Short); Nep. Att. 18.5: attigit quoque poēticēn

    Poetry as an art or pursuit; Nepos and Pliny use the Greek form poēticē, poēticēs f..

  • poēsis, poēsis f. — poetry; a poet’s work

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.71: Anacreontis tōta poēsis est amātōria (Lewis & Short); Hor. AP 361; Traupman 168

  • carmina, carminum n. pl. — poems, verses, songs

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical

    Poems, especially as songs; the word for one’s own verses (see song). versūs facere is “write poetry” (Cic. Q. fr. 3.5, Lewis & Short s.v. faciō).

Examples

  • sponte suā carmen numerōs veniēbat ad aptōs, et quod temptābam scrībere versus erat

    of its own accord my song fell into the right rhythm, and whatever I tried to write came out as verseOv. Tr. 4.10.25–26

  • foliīs tantum nē carmina mandā, nē turbāta volent rapidīs lūdibria ventīs

    only don’t write your verses on leaves, in case they are scattered and fly off as playthings of the rushing windsVerg. A. 6.74–75

  • poēma facere

    to write a poemTraupman 168

See also poet, song, recite, compose.
